walkthroughs.body_html:
Health Psychology — a core area of A-Level Psychology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Health Psychology brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Health Psychology.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Why does the cognitive approach use INFERENCE?
options: Because cognitive psychologists guess instead of measuring.
Mental processes cannot be directly observed, so they are inferred from behaviour.
Because brain scans are unreliable.
No relationship.

mcqs.q: Asch's line study primarily demonstrates which type of conformity?
options: Internalisation of group beliefs.
Because brain scans are unreliable.
Normative social influence (compliance to fit in).
Informational social influence (believing others know better).

options: A strong negative relationship.
No relationship.
A weak relationship (because it is negative).
Because brain scans are unreliable.
